original_question: Do the known results for line arrangements in P^2 extend to arrangements in higher-dimensional projective space? In particular, if A is a hyperplane arrangement in P^n, can one give an explicit description of the graded Betti numbers of the Orlik-Terao algebra C(A) in terms of the geometry of A?
target_in_paper: Problem 2.7.2 in Section 2.7 ("Blow-ups of P^n and hyperplane arrangements"), with clarifying context from the setup immediately preceding it and from Section 3.11, especially Example 3.11.1.
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper's actual open problem. It correctly identifies the passage from line arrangements in P^2 to higher-dimensional projective arrangements, correctly focuses on hyperplane arrangements A in P^n, and correctly singles out the central question of whether one can explicitly describe the graded Betti numbers of the Orlik-Terao algebra C(A) in terms of the geometry of A. This is essentially the content of Problem 2.7.2.
missing_details: The paper works over the complex numbers: the ambient coefficient field for the Orlik-Terao construction in Section 2.7 is C.
To make the question stand-alone, one should specify that A consists of d projective hyperplanes H_i = V(alpha_i), where the alpha_i are linear forms.
The ambient graded ring should be stated: R = C[y_1, ..., y_d], with one variable y_i for each hyperplane H_i.

The Orlik-Terao ideal must be defined explicitly: for each linear dependence Lambda: sum_{j=1}^k c_{i_j} alpha_{i_j} = 0, one forms f_Lambda = sum_{j=1}^k c_{i_j} y_{i_1} ... hat(y_{i_j}) ... y_{i_k}, and I(A) is generated by all such f_Lambda.
The Orlik-Terao algebra should then be stated as C(A) = R / I(A).

If the question is to be fully self-contained, the graded Betti numbers should be identified as beta_{i,j}(C(A)) = dim_C Tor_i^R(C(A), C)_{i+j}; this is the indexing convention explicitly used later in Example 3.11.1.
The official problem includes the known bound reg C(A) <= n for A in P^n; this should be retained, since it motivates the sharper Betti-number question.

The paper's nearby context shows that some geometric structures (weak multinets/nets) produce determinantal equations and syzygies, but Example 3.11.1 shows that not all linear first syzygies come from components of R^1(A). So the desired description cannot be phrased too narrowly as a resonance-only question.
There are no extra homogeneity, nilpotency, degree-cutoff, or 'for all sufficiently large m' conditions hidden in this problem; the main omitted items are the setup and grading data above.
refined_question: Let A = {H_1, ..., H_d} be a complex projective hyperplane arrangement in P^n, with H_i = V(alpha_i), and let R = C[y_1, ..., y_d]. For each linear dependence Lambda: sum_{j=1}^k c_{i_j} alpha_{i_j} = 0 among the defining linear forms, define f_Lambda = sum_{j=1}^k c_{i_j} y_{i_1} ... hat(y_{i_j}) ... y_{i_k}, let I(A) be the ideal of R generated by all such f_Lambda, and set C(A) = R / I(A). It is known that reg C(A) <= n for A subset P^n. Do the results for arrangements of lines in P^2 generalize to higher dimension? More specifically, can one give an explicit description of the graded Betti numbers beta_{i,j}(C(A)) = dim_C Tor_i^R(C(A), C)_{i+j} in terms of the geometry of the arrangement A?
justification: The draft almost verbatim matches Problem 2.7.2. The missing content is the Section 2.7 setup defining the Orlik-Terao ideal/algebra and the fact that the question is posed over C with one polynomial variable per hyperplane. The official formulation also explicitly includes the known regularity bound reg C(A) <= n as motivation for asking for the full graded Betti table. Section 3.11 gives the relevant nearby precision about what 'geometry of A' is expected to mean in practice: nets and weak multinets produce determinantal equations and Eagon-Northcott-type syzygies, but Example 3.11.1 shows that not all linear first syzygies arise from components of R^1(A), so the open problem is genuinely broader than a resonance-only description.
